pack.name: Linux
pack.description: Everyday Linux terminal workflows: disks, files, processes, services, logs and networking
pack.author: sherpacli-community

commands.name: Find large files
commands.description: Show the largest files in the current directory tree.
commands.use_case: Use this to identify files that may be taking up too much disk space.

examples.description: List the largest files in the current folder

commands.name: Size of each folder
commands.description: Summarize disk usage of every entry in a directory, smallest to largest.
commands.use_case: Use when a disk is filling up and you need to know which folder is responsible.

examples.description: Check what is using space in /var

commands.name: Free space per filesystem
commands.description: Show used and available space for every mounted filesystem.
commands.use_case: Use for a quick look at how full each disk or partition is.

commands.name: List block devices
commands.description: Show disks, partitions and where they are mounted.
commands.use_case: Use before mounting, formatting or resizing a disk.

commands.name: Find files by name
commands.description: Search a directory tree for files matching a pattern.
commands.use_case: Use when you know part of a filename but not where it lives.

examples.description: Find every Dockerfile under the current folder

commands.name: Recently modified files
commands.description: List files changed within the last N days.
commands.use_case: Use to see what changed after an update or deploy.

commands.name: Detailed listing
commands.description: List files with permissions, owners, human-readable sizes and hidden files.
commands.use_case: Use to inspect a folder, including dotfiles.

commands.name: Create a symbolic link
commands.description: Point a new path at an existing file or directory.
commands.use_case: Use to expose a file in a second location without copying it.

commands.name: Make a file executable
commands.description: Add execute permission so a script can be run directly.
commands.use_case: Use after downloading or writing a shell script.

commands.name: Take ownership of a folder
commands.description: Recursively change owner and group to your user.
commands.use_case: Use when files were created by root (for example by a container) and you can no longer edit them.

examples.description: Fix ownership of a project folder

commands.name: Top processes by memory
commands.description: List the processes using the most memory.
commands.use_case: Use when the machine is slow or swapping.

commands.name: Find a process by name
commands.description: Show PIDs and full command lines matching a name.
commands.use_case: Use to get the PID of a program before inspecting or stopping it.

commands.name: Stop a process
commands.description: Ask a process to exit gracefully with SIGTERM.
commands.use_case: Use to stop a program that will not close normally.

commands.name: Force-kill a process
commands.description: Terminate a process immediately with SIGKILL. It gets no chance to clean up.
commands.use_case: Use only when a graceful kill did not work.

commands.name: What is using a port
commands.description: Show which process is listening on a TCP or UDP port.
commands.use_case: Use when a server fails with 'address already in use'.

commands.name: Show IP addresses
commands.description: Brief list of network interfaces and their addresses.
commands.use_case: Use to find your machine's local IP.

commands.name: Check if a host is reachable
commands.description: Send a few ICMP pings and report latency and loss.
commands.use_case: Use as a first step when a service seems unreachable.

commands.name: Look up DNS records
commands.description: Resolve a domain and print only the answers.
commands.use_case: Use to check DNS changes or debug name resolution.

commands.name: Service status
commands.description: Show whether a systemd service is running, plus its latest log lines.
commands.use_case: Use when a background service is not behaving.

commands.name: Restart a service
commands.description: Stop and start a systemd service.
commands.use_case: Use after changing a service's configuration.

commands.name: Follow a service's logs
commands.description: Stream new journal entries for one systemd unit.
commands.use_case: Use while reproducing a problem with a service. Press r to run it, since preview stops after 10 seconds.

commands.name: Errors since boot
commands.description: Show journal entries with priority error or worse from the current boot.
commands.use_case: Use to spot failing services or hardware after a restart.

commands.name: Follow a log file
commands.description: Print new lines as they are appended to a file.
commands.use_case: Use to watch an application log in real time.

commands.name: Create a .tar.gz archive
commands.description: Compress a folder into a gzip tarball.
commands.use_case: Use to back up or ship a directory.

commands.name: Extract a .tar.gz archive
commands.description: Unpack a gzip tarball into the current folder.
commands.use_case: Use after downloading a release or backup.

commands.name: Kernel and OS version
commands.description: Print the kernel version, architecture and distribution name.
commands.use_case: Use when reporting a bug or checking compatibility.

commands.name: Memory usage
commands.description: Show total, used and available RAM and swap.
commands.use_case: Use to check whether the system is short on memory.

commands.name: Uptime and load
commands.description: Show how long the system has been up and its load averages.
commands.use_case: Use for a quick health check of a server.
